topic.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
topic.summary: The product, power, and change of base properties for logarithms, the natural logarithm, and how horizontal dilations of logarithmic functions become vertical translations and dilations.

variants.stem: Let f(x) = log₅(25x).

parts.prompt: Write f(x) in the form a + log_b x by finding a.
Write an expression for f(x) as a constant plus a logarithm of x.
The graph of f is obtained from the graph of y = log₅(x) by which horizontal dilation?

fields.label: Dilation:
options: a horizontal compression by a factor of 1/25
a vertical stretch by a factor of 25
a horizontal stretch by a factor of 25
fields.key: a horizontal compression by a factor of 1/25

solution: By the product property, log₅(25x) = log₅(25) + log₅(x). Since 5² = 25, log₅(25) = 2, so f(x) = 2 + log₅(x) and a = 2.
f(x) = 2 + log₅(x).
Multiplying the input by 25 is a horizontal compression by a factor of 1/25. By the product property, this is the same graph as the graph of y = log₅(x) translated up 2 units.

variants.stem: Use the change of base property of logarithms.

parts.prompt: Use ln to approximate log₇(16). Round your answer to three decimal places.
The function g(x) = log₈₁ x can be written as g(x) = k log₃ x. Find k.
Which expression is equal to log_b x, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1?

solution: By the change of base property, log₈₁ x = (log₃ x)/(log₃(81)) = (log₃ x)/4, so k = 1/4.
The change of base property states that log_b x = (log_a x)/(log_a b). With a = e, log_b x = (ln x)/(ln b).

variants.stem: Write each expression as a single logarithm.
solution: By the power property, 4 log₂ x = log₂(x⁴). By the product property, log₂(x⁴) + log₂ 3 = log₂(3x⁴).
By the power property, 4 log₃(x − 1) = log₃((x − 1)⁴). By the quotient property, the expression equals log₃(x/(x − 1)⁴).

2 ln 9 − ln 3 = ln 9² − ln 3 = ln 81 − ln 3 = ln(81/3) = ln 27.

variants.stem: Expand each logarithm using the product, quotient, and power properties.
solution: By the product property, log₅(3x²) = log₅ 3 + log₅(x²). By the power property, log₅(x²) = 2 log₅ x.
By the quotient property, log₂(x²/y³) = log₂(x²) − log₂(y³). By the power property, this is 2 log₂ x − 3 log₂ y.
By the product property, ln(x³(x + 5)²) = ln(x³) + ln((x + 5)²). By the power property, this is 3 ln x + 2 ln(x + 5).

variants.stem: Expand each logarithm using the product, quotient, and power properties.
solution: By the product property, log₃(2x³) = log₃ 2 + log₃(x³). By the power property, log₃(x³) = 3 log₃ x.
By the quotient property, log₅(x²/y²) = log₅(x²) − log₅(y²). By the power property, this is 2 log₅ x − 2 log₅ y.
By the product property, ln(x²(x − 4)²) = ln(x²) + ln((x − 4)²). By the power property, this is 2 ln x + 2 ln(x − 4).

variants.stem: Expand each logarithm using the product, quotient, and power properties.
solution: By the product property, log₅(2x³) = log₅ 2 + log₅(x³). By the power property, log₅(x³) = 3 log₅ x.
By the quotient property, log₃(x³/y⁵) = log₃(x³) − log₃(y⁵). By the power property, this is 3 log₃ x − 5 log₃ y.
By the product property, ln(x³(x − 4)⁴) = ln(x³) + ln((x − 4)⁴). By the power property, this is 3 ln x + 4 ln(x − 4).

variants.stem: Expand each logarithm using the product, quotient, and power properties.
solution: By the product property, log₅(2x⁴) = log₅ 2 + log₅(x⁴). By the power property, log₅(x⁴) = 4 log₅ x.
By the quotient property, log₃(x³/y²) = log₃(x³) − log₃(y²). By the power property, this is 3 log₃ x − 2 log₃ y.
By the product property, ln(x²(x + 4)³) = ln(x²) + ln((x + 4)³). By the power property, this is 2 ln x + 3 ln(x + 4).

variants.stem: Expand each logarithm using the product, quotient, and power properties.

variants.stem: All logarithmic functions are vertical dilations of each other.

parts.prompt: The function g(x) = log₆₂₅ x can be written as g(x) = k log₅ x. Find k.

solution: By the change of base property, log₆₂₅ x = (log₅ x)/(log₅(625)) = (log₅ x)/4. So k = 1/4, and the graph of g is a vertical dilation of the graph of y = log₅ x by a factor of 1/4.
